fields.title: Polka: the field that needs to be renamed
fields.summary: The `total` field needs to start including delivery. All 900 partners are on v1.
fields.decisionPrompt: How do we run the change? Name the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a customer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a Polka partner API PM. The contract has a `total` field—the order amount. Historically it did not include delivery, and documentation states this in one line. Finance asks to change it: starting next year, commission is calculated from the amount including delivery, and partners must see the same figure as in the invoice. Right now their numbers drift, and this has already led to two commission disputes. Deadline is end of quarter, six weeks.
fields.brief/objective: Bring the figure in the API in line with the invoice by January 1 without silently breaking those who rely on it.
fields.brief/constraints: Six weeks. The previous v1 → v2 migration took eight months.
fields.brief/task: Decide how you run the change and what you tell partners.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Compatibility is broken explicitly or silently—no third option
fields.learnTakeaway/body: Changing the meaning of a field does not break the format, so it looks cheap: nobody crashes. Figures crash for those who trust you, and they find out weeks later. The right move is a new field alongside, a deprecation deadline for the old one, and targeted work with those who actually use it. A field usage counter turns "we don't know who uses this" into a list of three hundred forty names.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: 900 partners. On `v1`—all. Actively use the `total` field—340 partners based on logs.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: "Changing the meaning of `total` takes three days. Adding `total_with_delivery` alongside takes three days. Releasing `v2` with new semantics takes three weeks plus supporting two versions. A usage counter by field exists, by partner too."
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: The transition `v1` → `v2` during inventory structure changes took eight months and required targeted work with 11 partners.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Starting January 1, discrepancy in invoices becomes systemic: two disputes last quarter took 30 hours of accounting time.
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Three days. The field starts including delivery, documentation is updated.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: we make it with a huge margin. Nothing crashes—format is the same. For 340 partners, numbers silently change, for 6 chains, automatic reconciliation breaks. They will discover it weeks later, trust will suffer more than from an honest crash.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Three days plus communication. Both fields live, old one marked, no removal deadline set.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: we make it. Nothing breaks. Partners switch whenever they want—some will never switch. The contract acquires two fields with similar names, which is a source of errors in itself. Financial problem solved for those who switched.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Release `v2` with new semantics, migration window
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Release `v2` with new semantics, migration window. Three weeks plus months for migration.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: clean contractually. Does not meet January 1: past experience shows migration takes months, not weeks. Expensive for a single-field change.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: `total_with_delivery` plus targeted work with 340 active consumers and a deadline
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: `total_with_delivery` plus targeted work with 340 active consumers and a 9-month removal deadline for `total`. Three days of work plus a campaign.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: we meet the deadline, financial problem is solved as adoption happens. Contract ends up clean. Requires partner work and a solution for 3 uncontacted chains. Does not instantly solve the commission dispute for those who haven't switched.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Fails to recognize meaning change as breaking
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Fails to plan a migration window with measurement
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Fails to distinguish consumers by significance
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: API contract is read as a set of fields rather than a promise to a partner
fields.rubric/remediation/4/gap: Removal of old field not formalized with a deadline and warning
